ca-start.speaker: S01
ca-start.narration: Lady Constance does not offer you a seat. You take one anyway.
ca-start.text: Thirty-three years I kept this house for him, and he left it to Gerald. You may ask your questions. I may not answer them.

ca-will.speaker: S01
ca-will.narration: Her knuckles whiten on the arm of the chair.
ca-will.text: An annuity. For his wife. And everything else to a brother he hadn't spoken to in ten years. Gerald was going to put me in the dower cottage by Christmas. I'm not sorry he's dead. I didn't kill him.

ca-gerald.speaker: S01
ca-gerald.text: Insufferable, loud, and suddenly rich. He spent the first half of the reading telling Ambrose he'd have the trust accounts gone through by Monday. Poor Ambrose looked quite ill.

ca-fairlie.speaker: S01
ca-fairlie.text: Ambrose has been our solicitor for thirty years. The only honest man in this house. He sat and read that dreadful document without a tremor.

ca-nurse.speaker: S01
ca-nurse.text: Agnes kept all of Edmund's pills. Heart pills. She's a good girl, but she'd been promised money and she didn't get any. I only tell you what's true.

ca-e004.speaker: S01
ca-e004.narration: For a moment she looks her age.
ca-e004.text: My saccharin. I'm diabetic, and I will not have the staff handling my medicine. I fetch it myself at ten to four every day. I didn't say because it's nobody's business but mine.

ca-unmoved.speaker: S01
ca-unmoved.text: I have no idea what that is, and I don't intend to find out.

am-start.speaker: S02
am-start.narration: Agnes Mora keeps her hands in her apron pockets.
am-start.text: Everyone keeps asking about the Colonel's pills. I know what it looks like. I nursed him for a year. I'd never hurt anybody.

choices.label: Ask about the Colonel's last months
Ask what happened to his medicines
Ask where she was during the reading

am-colonel.speaker: S02
am-colonel.text: His heart was failing. Digoxin every morning, a quarter of a milligram. He used to say it tasted of nothing, and so it does. He promised me something in the will. He forgot, I suppose.

am-pills.speaker: S02
am-pills.text: I destroyed them. After he died. That's the rule. I haven't had any digoxin since June.

am-tea.speaker: S02
am-tea.text: Up here, with the laundry. Nurses don't sit with the family, and nobody invited me to hear a will I wasn't in.

am-e008.speaker: S02
am-e008.narration: She reads her own signature and then the one underneath it.
am-e008.text: I didn't destroy them. I kept them too long, and then Mr Fairlie said they were estate property and must go on the probate inventory. I handed him every tablet, all sixty, on the tenth. He put the box in his car with the other inventory things. I lied because I'd broken the rules. I'm sorry.

am-e002.speaker: S02
am-e002.text: Tablets. Not foxglove. So it was his. The Colonel's. Oh, God.

am-unmoved.speaker: S02
am-unmoved.text: I don't know anything about that. I only looked after the Colonel.

sb-start.speaker: S03
sb-start.narration: Silas Brook snips a rose and drops it in the trug before he looks at you.
sb-start.text: You'll have seen the foxgloves. Everybody's seen the foxgloves. Go on, then.

variants.text: I've nothing more to say to you. Forty years I've kept this garden. Get off my border.

choices.label: Accuse him of poisoning Gerald with foxglove

sb-afternoon.speaker: S03
sb-afternoon.text: Walled garden, three till five. Tying in the sweet peas. I never came near the house.

sb-foxgloves.speaker: S03
sb-foxgloves.text: I cut them for the house every July. Her ladyship likes them. If I wanted to poison a man I wouldn't put the evidence in a vase on his tea table.

sb-gerald.speaker: S03
sb-gerald.text: Told me I'd be pensioned off before the autumn. Forty years. I'd have gone quiet, mind. I'm too old to hang for a pension.

sb-accused.speaker: S03
sb-accused.narration: He puts the secateurs down very carefully.
sb-accused.text: Forty years. Forty years, and a man in a raincoat calls me a poisoner in my own garden. You'll get nothing more out of me.

sb-e005.speaker: S03
sb-e005.text: All right, I went round to the drive. The wine van couldn't get past Mr Fairlie's car. And there he was, ten past four, come out of the house like a man in a hurry, head in the glovebox of that Humber. Jumped like a cat when he saw me. Said he'd come for his spectacles. He was wearing them.

af-start.speaker: S04
af-start.narration: Ambrose Fairlie folds his reading glasses and sets them square on his papers.
af-start.text: Detective. A wretched business. I've known this family for thirty years, and I read that will to them myself. Whatever you need.

variants.narration: His clerk has been and gone. So has his briefcase.
variants.text: My papers are privileged, Detective. My clerk has taken them back to the office. I'm sure you understand.

choices.label: Demand to see inside his briefcase

af-reading.speaker: S04
af-reading.text: I began at four and read until Gerald fell. I never left the room, and I never touched the tea things; Mrs Hobbs saw to all that. I was rather occupied with the codicils.

af-tea.speaker: S04
af-tea.text: Mrs Hobbs, I imagine. Or Gerald helped himself; he generally did. I was reading, Detective. I didn't see.

af-trust.speaker: S04
af-trust.text: In perfect order. I've kept those accounts for twenty-two years. Gerald wanted to go through them, which was his right as executor. I'd have been glad to help him.

af-widow.speaker: S04
af-widow.narration: He chooses his words with care.
af-widow.text: Dear Constance was disinherited at that table, in front of us all. She took it very hard. She left the room once before the reading. I say no more than that.

af-nurse.speaker: S04
af-nurse.text: The nurse had charge of the Colonel's heart medicine. If I were you, I'd ask her very plainly what became of it.

af-briefcase.speaker: S04
af-briefcase.narration: He rings the bell for his clerk.
af-briefcase.text: Those papers are privileged, Detective. You'll need a warrant, and you won't get one by tonight. Mr Pardoe will take them back to the office.

af-e004.speaker: S04
af-e004.text: Mrs Hobbs is mistaken. Or I may have handed Gerald his cup. It's a courtesy. People do it without thinking.

af-e008.speaker: S04
af-e008.text: For the probate inventory. Purely a formality. They were to be destroyed. I'd quite forgotten.

af-e007.speaker: S04
af-e007.narration: He looks at the bottle, and then at nothing at all.
af-e007.text: Forty-two. You've counted them. Of course you've counted them.

af-e011.speaker: S04
af-e011.text: That is private correspondence between a trustee and his bank. A temporary shortfall. It would have been put right.

af-e006.speaker: S04
af-e006.text: I stepped out for my spectacles. Two minutes. An old man forgets his spectacles, Detective.

af-unmoved.speaker: S04
af-unmoved.text: I'm afraid I can't help you with that one, Detective.

ra-start.speaker: S05
ra-start.narration: Rory Ashcombe pushes his pint an inch away from him.
ra-start.text: The black sheep turns up the day the heir drops dead. I'd suspect me too. I wasn't even in the house.

choices.label: Ask what he saw from the library

ra-why.speaker: S05
ra-why.text: To find out if Uncle Edmund had forgiven me before he died. He hadn't. Not a penny.

ra-when.speaker: S05
ra-when.text: Half past four. By the time I walked up the drive the doctor's car was already outside.

ra-fairlie.speaker: S05
ra-fairlie.text: Fairlie stopped my allowance five years ago. Said the trust couldn't afford me. Funny, that; the trust was worth half a million.

ra-e015.speaker: S05
ra-e015.text: All right. Half-three bus. I went up to the Hall and hid in the library to listen at the door, to hear if I was in the will. The maid saw me. I never went in the drawing room. I ran when Gerald fell.

ra-saw.speaker: S05
ra-saw.text: At ten past four old Fairlie came out of the drawing room white as a sheet and went straight out to his car. I saw him through the library window. He was back in five minutes, and then Mrs Hobbs brought the tea.
